chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdullah ibn Muskhan from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'There is no zakat in debt,' and he said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Is zakat due on money owed to you as a debt before you receive it?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the obligation of zakat does not accrue on outstanding debts (*dayn*) while they remain unpaid, distinguishing this state from possessed wealth. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic consensus that zakat is levied on actual possession (*qabd*) rather than mere entitlement, ensuring that the financial burden does not compound for the debtor who may lack liquidity. The narration underscores the practical mercy in Islamic finance, preventing the double burden of debt repayment and zakat on uncollected funds.
